newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RBA says no fee on repos through RTGS system.
newsitem.headline: RBA says no fee on repos through RTGS system.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) said it will stand ready to provide intra-day liquidity to banks and others with Exchange Settlement Accounts to ensure that payments flow smoothly through the planned Real-Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) system.
This liquidity will take the form of within-day repurchase agreements in Commonwealth Government Securities, it said.

The RBA's initial intention was to impose a fee of 10 basis points per annum on these repurchase agreements but, following discussion with industry partipants, the central bank has now decided that it will provide liquidity free of charge.
The transaction fee will be the same as that applying to mortgages, and will amount to A$3 per line of stock per leg of each transaction.

"This decision should ensure that there is no obstacle to banks and others being able to generate a steady supply of liquidity to support the RTGS system which is due to commence in the first half of 1998," the RBA said in a statement.
"The bank will keep arrangements under review to ensure that they do not undermine its control over monetary conditions," it added.
